claims.text: Low-temperature annealing of FeMnNiCoCr promotes the formation of short-range-order clusters.
Introducing short-range order into FeMnNiCoCr increases its yield strength relative to a high-temperature-homogenized baseline.
Introducing short-range order alters the deformation behavior of FeMnNiCoCr.
Short-range order impedes dislocation motion in FeMnNiCoCr.
The initial homogenized FeMnNiCoCr alloy is a fully disordered solid solution.
Rapid quenching after low-temperature annealing preserves the annealing-induced short-range order for subsequent testing.
The relevant structural mediator is the presence, density, and distribution of short-range-order clusters.
Electron diffraction and atom probe tomography can determine the relevant short-range-order characteristics.
Short-range-order clusters act as nanoscale obstacles to dislocation glide.
Short-range-order clusters increase the energy barriers for dislocation motion.
Increased barriers to dislocation motion elevate yield strength.
Increased barriers to dislocation motion modify strain-rate sensitivity.
FeMnNiCoCr with pronounced short-range order will have reduced dislocation mobility relative to the homogenized baseline.
High-temperature homogenization produces a FeMnNiCoCr baseline lacking significant short-range order.
The proposed mechanism should apply at room temperature when thermal treatments modify short-range order without inducing secondary phase transformations.
Competing microstructural effects may obscure the isolated mechanical contribution of short-range order.
The hypothesis is falsified if confirmed short-range order produces no statistically significant mechanical differences and no reduced dislocation mobility relative to the homogenized baseline.

contradictions.description: The predicted-outcome field says any lack of correlation between mechanical properties and measured SRO would falsify the hypothesis, whereas the formal rule is narrower and requires no statistically significant mechanical differences plus absence of reduced dislocation mobility despite confirmed SRO.
